 The Honourable Sri Justice N. Tukaramji

Order:

This petition is filed seeking quashment of the C.C.No.377 of 2021 on the file of learned Principal Junior Civil Judge-cum-IV Additional Judicial Magistrate of the First Class, Medchal-Malkajgiri District at L.B.Nagar, against the petitioners/accused Nos.2, 3 7 and 9.

entities.text: Principal Junior Civil Judge-cum-IV Additional Judicial Magistrate of the First Class, Medchal-Malkajgiri District at L.B.Nagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
[
2. Heard Mr.Syed Tousif Basha, learned counsel for petitioners and Mr.Jithender Rao Veeramalla,
learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing for the respondent No.1-State.

3. The petitioners are arrayed as accused Nos.2, 3 7 and 9 in C.C.No.377 of 2021 for the offences under Sections 498 (A), 494, 420, 323 and 506 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry and Prohibition Act, 1961.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioners would submit that though the petitioners are resolved to face the proceedings, their presence before the trial Court on each adjournment is causing severe hardship and effecting their employment.
Therefore, prayed for dispensing their personal presence unless it is required for the proceedings and such direction would redress their grievance.

5. Learned Additional Public Prosecutor submits that there is no specific objection for the prayer,
however pleaded for a direction for in person presence of the petitioners in the material stages of the proceedings.
6.

Having regard to the submissions, subject to the petitioners' appearance through their counsel on every adjournment and the petitioners' personal appearance as and when directed by the Court, the personal presence of the petitioners in the proceedings of the C.C.No.377 of 2021 on the file of learned Principal Junior Civil Judge- cum-IV Additional Judicial Magistrate of the First Class,
Medchal- Malkajgiri District at L.B.Nagar, is dispensed with.
Additionally it is specified that any lapse in abiding the above conditions would render this order ineffective.
7. With this direction, this Criminal Petition is disposed of.
Miscellaneous petitions, pending if any, shall stand closed.
Raghava Singh vs The State Of Telangana.
